0.long_answer: DOORS syndrome is a rare genetic disorder that is characterized by a combination of features including sensorineural deafness, intellectual disability, and abnormalities in the bones of the fingers and toes. The name DOORS is an acronym reflecting several of the major characteristics of the syndrome: Deafness, Onychodystrophy (abnormal or underdeveloped nails), Osteodystrophy (abnormal bone development), intellectual Disability, and seizures. This condition is identified through a combination of clinical findings and genetic testing, and management is typically multidisciplinary aimed at addressing the various symptoms and improving quality of life.
